summary: Milestone 2026.09.671 completed 12 experiments, all compute-bound, totaling 40.7 wall-time minutes (average 3 minutes per experiment) with timing reconstructed via disk-mtime fallback. Execution time was dominated by 'Qualify causal constraint acquisition with a hard proposal budget' at 21.0 minutes, followed by 'Measure live goal evidence during adapter-withheld first contact' at 8.85 minutes and 'Measure explicit record and claim addressing with bounded Qwen proposals' at 4.67 minutes. Together, the top three compute-bound tasks accounted for 34.52 of the 40.7 total wall-time minutes (84.8%), while intra-task phase durations were unmeasured.
bottlenecks_identified: The slowest experiment ('Qualify causal constraint acquisition with a hard proposal budget') required 21.0 minutes, consuming 51.6% of the 40.7 total milestone wall-time minutes alone, but the lack of sub-phase profiling prevents isolating time spent on model inference versus proposal budgeting and constraint evaluation.

The top three slowest compute-bound experiments ('Qualify causal constraint acquisition with a hard proposal budget' at 21.0 minutes, 'Measure live goal evidence during adapter-withheld first contact' at 8.85 minutes, and 'Measure explicit record and claim addressing with bounded Qwen proposals' at 4.67 minutes) accounted for 34.52 of 40.7 total minutes (84.8%), representing extreme execution concentration without intra-task stage breakdown.

The post-run GPU monitor report captures an idle state (GPU 0 at 5MB, 0% util; GPU 1 at 4MB, 0% util) at milestone completion, but because gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is false, this reflects post-run quiescence rather than an active-task bottleneck; continuous in-run GPU telemetry across active task windows was absent.
No experiment records indicate concurrent execution of two or more models in parallel, so DualGPURunner dispatch was not applicable to the single-model tasks executed this milestone.
Timing data required disk-mtime reconstruction fallback because the live git-log path found 0 commits, precluding commit-anchored execution timestamps.
improvements_suggested: Instrument fine-grained sub-phase monotonic timers within long-running compute-bound tasks—particularly causal constraint acquisition and live goal evidence routines—to decompose proposal generation time from constraint validation.
Capture continuous active-window GPU utilization and VRAM metrics during compute-bound executions to evaluate accelerator efficiency throughout task runs.
Persist model concurrency and runner dispatch metadata in experiment receipts to formally verify DualGPURunner applicability on multi-model workloads.
Emit synchronous, structured start and finish timestamps directly to experiment execution receipts to avoid falling back to filesystem disk-mtime reconstruction.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument sub-phase duration profiling inside causal constraint acquisition and adapter evaluation loops to isolate model inference latency from constraint logic.
Deploy continuous in-task GPU utilization monitoring during compute-bound runs to capture active-window accelerator throughput.
Persist structured execution lifecycle timestamps and model concurrency metadata directly into task receipts to ensure robust timing and runner auditability.
meta_reflection: Milestone 2026.09.671 executed 12 compute-bound tasks across 40.7 wall-time minutes, with 84.8% of runtime concentrated in the top three experiments led by causal constraint acquisition at 21.0 minutes and live goal evidence at 8.85 minutes. While the post-run GPU monitor snapshot recorded both RTX 3090 GPUs idle (5MB/4MB allocated, 0% utilization), gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is false and active-window accelerator efficiency was not continuously logged, with no multi-model tasks present to engage DualGPURunner. Implementing fine-grained sub-phase timing and continuous accelerator telemetry represents the most effective operational path to isolating bottlenecks in upcoming compute-heavy milestones.
